items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Then after we was in Baltimore, Roy Eldridge joined the band... And we played at Carlin's Park all that summer... So Roy and I used to go jamming everytime we got off work.

ctx.x: Sy was writing. In fact, Sy was the band. And Sy was the Jimmy Lunceford band. I mean, Sy took all of this stuff from one place to the other and it was Sy Oliver. I mean, you have to give him credit for that. He had developed a style and it became a great style of writing. And he took it from Zach White and took it to Jimmy Lunceford. And then he left Jimmy Lunceford and took it to Tommy Dorsey's band.

So I stayed with Zach up until I got sick in Chattanooga, Tennessee and they left me there. Left me in Chattanooga. I stayed in Chattanooga about two, three months, recuperating, then I got a telegram to join McKinney's Cotton Pickers. And I went up to Pennsylvania to play with them. And while I was with the band they all got together and fired McKinney. And we went to Baltimore to work at Carlin's Park (PHONETIC). Then after we was in Baltimore, Roy Eldridge joined the band. And that was me and -- the reed…

items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: It was just like in the old days with the gunfighters... Roy Eldridges and the Jabbo Smiths and the Louis Armstrongs and all of these trumpet players...

ctx.x: He took care of Prince Robinson?

He took care of everybody. But that was the way it was. It was just like in the old days with the gunfighters. One guy had to be better and this was the way the musicians really learned how to play. Roy Eldridges
and the Jabbo Smiths and the Louis Armstrongs and all of these trumpet players, Dizzy Gillespies and Charlie Shaffers. I mean, this was the thing.
